blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Interactive video generation commonly relies on small bidirectional chunks to reduce response latency. Yet our preliminary experiments show that larger chunks improve video quality and better utilize GPU parallelism, allowing more latents to be sampled with only a modest increase in sampling time. Motivated by these observations, we propose Speculative Sampling, a strategy that combines the modeling power of large bidirectional windows with the low-latency interaction of small ones. It expands the modeling window by appending noise latents as padding and caches the resulting predictions for reuse when the condition remains unchanged. Predictions are delivered incrementally, while the uncommitted future remains replaceable. Our latency analysis shows that this removes the waiting-time lower bound imposed by chunk boundaries, shifting the optimization focus from reducing chunk size to accelerating per-chunk sampling. Bidirectional window size thus becomes a decision variable for jointly optimizing visual quality and sampling time, rather than a necessary constraint on low-latency interaction. This opens a path to serving large bidirectional models in interactive streaming systems without complex streaming post-training.
blocks.zh: 互动视频生成通常依靠小的双向块来降低响应延迟. 然而,我们的初步实验表明,更大的块提高了视频质量,并更好地利用了GPU的平行性,使得更多的潜伏物能够取样,而采样时间却略有增加。 基于这些观察,我们提出分镜抽样,这个策略将大型双向窗口的建模功率与小型窗口的低相关性相互作用结合起来. 它通过附加噪声潜伏物来扩展建模窗口,作为粘贴,并缓存由此产生的预测,以便在条件保持不变时再利用。 预测是逐步提供的,而未承诺的未来仍然可以取代。 我们的耐久性分析显示,这消除了块边界造成的等待时间下限,将优化重点从缩小块大小转移到加速每块取样。 因此,双向窗口大小成为共同优化视觉质量和取样时间的决定变量,而不是对低相关性互动的必要限制。 这开启了一条在互动流式系统中服务大型双向模型而无需复杂的流式后培训的道路.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Interactive video generation requires newly arriving conditions to influence
ongoing playback promptly. A viewer may change a camera command or action
instruction at any time, while existing video continues to play.
Generation throughput alone does not capture this requirement: a fast model
can still leave the viewer waiting for a generation or playback boundary.

blocks.en:
A natural route is fine-grained autoregressive generation. Advances in
rollout training and few-step distillation have made this route increasingly
practical ( Huang et al., 2025 ; Zhao et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2025 ) .
Smaller generation chunks provide more frequent opportunities to incorporate
new conditions, enabling fine-grained interaction, but may limit joint
temporal modeling and parallel efficiency.
This raises our central question: must low-latency interaction come at
the cost of a smaller bidirectional modeling window?

blocks.en:
We first formulate a serving model that separates condition arrivals,
generation, output commitment, and playback. Generation is the computation
needed for deliverable video output; for the latent diffusion models studied
here, it includes DiT sampling and required VAE decoding. The model distinguishes
generation time from phase-dependent random-arrival waiting imposed
by scheduling and playback boundaries, and identifies replaceable outputs.
When new output can enter playback only at chunk boundaries, the chunk
duration imposes a waiting floor even if generation is fast.

We next examine chunk size K K , the number of latent frames jointly
sampled in one DiT sampling call. Changing K K affects joint temporal modeling
and parallel efficiency, as well as the time needed to generate each chunk.
Our chunk-size ablation shows higher aggregate video
quality for larger-chunk configurations than their frame-wise counterparts
in the evaluated settings (Section 4 ). Larger chunks also
better utilize GPU parallelism, allowing more latents to be sampled with only
a modest increase in sampling time. Together with the
system model, this motivates retaining the benefits of joint generation
while reducing the waiting imposed by coarse output commitment.

blocks.en:
Guided by the system model and chunk-size ablation, we develop our method to
combine large-chunk joint generation with fine-grained delivery.
We expand the bidirectional modeling window by appending noise latents as
padding. Rather than discarding the resulting predictions, we cache them for
reuse when the condition remains unchanged, while keeping the uncommitted
future replaceable.
We formulate the controller as a two-state finite-state machine that
coordinates joint generation and incremental consumption of cached
predictions, while playback continues independently.
This decouples DiT sampling calls from individual deliveries: completed
predictions are reused between condition updates, avoiding repeated
sampling merely to support finer-grained delivery.

The resulting design points to an alternative route to interactive video
generation: shrinking chunks need not be a prerequisite for low interaction
latency. Instead, the optimization focus can shift to accelerating
high-quality joint generation.
DiT sampling acceleration and parallel acceleration can support this route.
We further demonstrate this route by serving a large bidirectional model in a
low-latency interactive streaming system without Self-Forcing-style
post-training.

Our contributions are fourfold: 1. A simple serving-system model for interactive video generation. We formalize condition arrivals, generation, output commitment, and
playback, distinguishing generation time from the additional waiting
imposed by scheduling and playback boundaries
(Section 3.1 ). 2. A systematic analysis of chunk size. We study how chunk size affects video quality, generation
time, and redundant computation, clarifying the trade-offs between joint
modeling and responsiveness (Section 4 ;
Appendices A – B ). 3. Recomputation-efficient speculative sampling. Guided by this model and analysis, we propose a speculative sampling
scheme formulated as a two-state finite-state machine.
It combines large-chunk joint generation with fine-grained output
commitment, reusing predictions and replanning only
a feasible suffix when conditions change (Section 3 ). 4. An alternative route to interactive video generation. By separating chunk size from output commitment, we shift
the optimization focus from shrinking chunks to accelerating high-quality
joint generation, making per-chunk generation time a central target

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Autoregressive video generation exploits temporal structure by predicting new
content conditioned on the past ( Yan et al., 2021 ) . This provides a
natural interface for extending videos, including segment-wise continuation
under changing prompts ( Villegas et al., 2022 ) . Bringing sequential
prediction to diffusion models ( Chen et al., 2024 ) leaves two
practical challenges: the cost of repeated sampling and errors accumulated
through generated history. Recent progress therefore targets efficient
few-step causal generation ( Yin et al., 2024 ; Zhao et al., 2026 ) and training
aligned with self-generated, long-horizon rollouts ( Huang et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2025 ) . Related rolling and bidirectional-window
approaches retain joint temporal processing during sequential output ( Kim et al., 2024 ; Kodaira et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2025 ; Rui et al., 2026 ) .
NFD additionally describes speculative multi-frame sampling on a frame-causal
backbone to improve throughput, but retains a causal mask within the enlarged
window and therefore does not exploit bidirectional modeling across it ( Cheng et al., 2025 ) . Related control mechanisms
include reuse or replanning of fully denoised futures with ground-truth
observation feedback ( Lillemark et al., 2026 ) and management of generation–playback
lead ( Bai et al., 2026 ) . Our method studies a complementary interface:
retaining temporally bidirectional joint generation within each chunk while committing
outputs at a finer granularity under newly arriving conditions.

blocks.en:
Acceleration targets several components of generation cost. Few-step
distillation ( Yin et al., 2024 ; Zhao et al., 2026 ) and adversarial post-training ( Lin et al., 2025 ) reduce DiT sampling steps. Pyramid Flow performs
much of its DiT sampling below full spatial resolution and compresses history
through a temporal pyramid ( Jin et al., 2024 ) ; FramePack reduces the
historical-context token budget ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) .
FasterCache and TeaCache reuse intermediate computations across diffusion
steps ( Lv et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2024 ) , whereas Sliding Tile Attention
and Sparse VideoGen reduce attention work through local or spatial–temporal
sparsity ( Zhang et al., 2025b ; Xi et al., 2025 ) . USP addresses distributed attention
through sequence parallelism ( Fang and Zhao, 2024 ) . These methods have distinct
training and inference requirements. Our perspective shifts the emphasis
from shrinking generation chunks to accelerating their generation. By
decoupling generation from output commitment, our method highlights per-chunk
generation time, rather than chunk size alone, as a key determinant of
interaction latency. This places greater importance on accelerating joint
generation instead of requiring increasingly fine-grained autoregressive
models.

blocks.en:
Bidirectional teacher models often define the quality target for causal
streaming students, yet their full-sequence generation interfaces are not
designed for interactive serving. Directly converting the same backbone
to causal generation can also introduce a quality gap without careful
adaptation ( Yin et al., 2024 ) . This motivates a further extrapolation
of chunk size: can a large-chunk bidirectional model itself serve an
interactive video stream? We preserve bidirectional joint sampling within
each call and adapt its conditioning and output interfaces, allowing
successive calls to continue from retained video while outputs are
committed incrementally.

blocks.en:
Bidirectional video generators commonly provide native image- or
video-conditioned continuation interfaces, allowing successive jointly
sampled chunks to be connected without modifying within-chunk attention.
A practical complication arises with
temporally compressive 3D VAEs: the continuation interface often expects a
temporally uncompressed first-frame latent, whereas an interior cached frame
belongs to a temporally compressed latent group. We therefore decode the
retained boundary to pixels and re-encode its final frame through the VAE’s
first-frame path before the next DiT sampling call. This produces the latent
format expected by the pretrained continuation interface. Alternatively,
the bidirectional model can be fine-tuned to accept compressed latent
continuation directly.

blocks.en:
The main limitations are twofold. First, our method benefits from predictions
only when they are reused before a new condition invalidates them; frequent or
continuous updates can therefore discard much of each sampled chunk and waste
substantial DiT computation. Second, with bidirectional within-chunk attention,
the retained KV may encode information from a subsequently discarded suffix,
so deleting its KV entries may not fully remove its influence on a regenerated
continuation.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion

blocks.en:
We have formulated interactive video generation as a joint problem of
prediction and output commitment. Our method preserves multi-latent joint generation,
reuses completed predictions under unchanged conditions, and replans only
the future that can still be replaced while maintaining a feasible playback
prefix. This shifts part of the design effort from shrinking the generation
unit toward accelerating joint generation, managing revocable predictions,
and scheduling timely delivery.

No delivered or locked prefix is overwritten. A new branch never directly
attends to invalid suffix entries. At most one job occupies the active slot,
and only a guarded launch starts new DiT sampling.
Playback and cache positions remain consistent after a
branch. No predicted latent is counted as displayed before a display event.
VAE decoder invalidation cannot alter already delivered pixel frames. Missed
deadlines, superseded updates, and additional work are recorded in the logs.

Each event log should include a run identifier, event identifier, condition
version, condition-ready time, prefix-ready time, generation start, KV-ready
time, DiT sampling completion, VAE decoding completion, first deliverable
output time, target switch boundary, actual display time, and final outcome.
Generation logs additionally record call
identifier, absolute positions, used and discarded predictions, runtime,
GPU count, and any canceled or repeated work. Model, DiT sampling, resolution,
frame-rate, and buffer configurations belong in run metadata. Record the
conditioning adapter, retained-context identity, source-to-playback offsets,
and trimmed overlap, so native image continuation is not conflated with
retained-prefix KV reuse.

blocks.en:
The controller operates on retained content and playback deadlines.
Its conditioning state ℋ j \mathcal{H}_{j} need not have the same representation
across generators. This section distinguishes the adapters used to expose
continuation, rather than treating all streaming paths as full-prefix KV
reuse.

它的构造状态为 H j\ mathcal{H}_{j} 不需要有相同的代表
跨发电机。 本节区分用于曝光的适配器
继续,而不是将所有流线路径当作全前缀 KV

blocks.en:
For a generator with history-conditioned DiT sampling, the adapter exposes
the selected prefix’s inference state at the correct positions.
Direct suffix entries are invalidated while the retained KV is reused.
This preserves the original inference representations; it does not
reconstruct them from clean latents. An implementation that instead builds
KV by clean prefill of each retained latent is a different cache policy.
An LTX proposal-reuse implementation may instead use incremental clean
prefill; that should be identified separately from direct retained-KV reuse.
Neither policy can erase old-future information already present in fixed
prefix latent values. Separating the additional effect of KV reuse requires
a matched controlled ablation.

blocks.en:
The bidirectional image-conditioned path retrieves the full-resolution
RGB frame immediately preceding the selected branch from the retained
timeline, then submits it through the checkpoint’s native image
conditioning interface with the latest available prompt.
The H3 image-conditioned path can implement this operation without a new
temporal causal mask or wrapper-specific training.
This path conditions on the boundary image rather than full-prefix KV or
equivalent long-range context.

blocks.en:
The H3 experimental latent-input path replaces image encoding with a
normalized clean video latent while retaining condition packing and
condition-noise handling. This differs from copying the latent into the target
noise tensor, and its conditioning distribution differs from that of a single
encoded image. A separate multi-frame path supplies a
phase-aligned group of retained latents as keyframe conditions and removes
the corresponding output overlap. These variants change context, eligible
boundaries, and preparation costs, and are reported separately from the
boundary-image adapter.

blocks.en:
A native clip may include a regenerated anchor or context span. The output
adapter omits that span and maps only the remaining pixels to the new
playback interval. It retains source indices for subsequent anchors, and
never selects history from a discarded or trimmed-away prediction.
This mapping can have nonuniform latent-to-frame spans and fewer playable
groups than sampled latents; the controller uses their actual deadlines.

blocks.en:
Streaming VAE decoding can publish finalized groups before the entire
clip has finished decoding, while DiT sampling remains joint over the
chunk. This does not imply that a prefix of bidirectional DiT sampling is
available early. VAE overlap and any state dependent on a replaced suffix
must be handled before pixels are committed; the adapter may instead
decode the full clip and deliver its completed frames incrementally.
Group-ready and job-finish events remain separate in both cases.
History encoding, cache construction, VAE decoding, and mandatory overlap
work are included in the corresponding timing and cost measurements.

在这两种情况下,小组准备和完成工作的活动仍然分开。

工作包括在相应的时间和费用衡量中。

blocks.en: Appendix F Future work: co-optimizing DiT sampling and VAE decoding
blocks.zh: 附录F 今后的工作:协同优化DiT取样和VAE解码

blocks.en:
Accelerating joint DiT sampling is one route to retaining large chunks,
but the serving objective is to reduce generation time C C to the
first deliverable output group. A natural next step is to co-design DiT
sampling and VAE decoding as a single generation pipeline rather than
optimize their isolated runtimes. This includes when completed latent groups
are handed to the VAE decoder, how decoding is scheduled against playback
deadlines, and how compute and memory are allocated between stages.
blocks.zh:
加速联合DiT采样是保留大块的一个途径,
但服务目标是将生产时间 C C 缩短到
第一个可交付产出组。 一个自然的下一步是共同设计DiT
取样和VAE解码作为单代管道而不是
优化他们孤立的运行时间。 这包括已完成的潜在组别
将解码器交给 VAE 解码器, 如何将解码安排在回放时
以及各阶段之间如何分配计算和内存。

blocks.en:
Overlap schedules must respect the data dependencies of temporally
bidirectional DiT sampling and VAE decoding. Candidate schedules should measure
time to the first deliverable group, later-group deadlines, total GPU cost,
and playback stalls. Parallel acceleration should be evaluated within the
complete pipeline and resource budget.

时间到第一个交付组, 后组期限, GPU 总成本,
和回放摊位。 应在
完成编审和资源预算。
